note: Receipts for verification this repository performs OUTSIDE continuous integration, because CI cannot perform it. Each entry names the protocol, the commit it was run at, and what came out. tools/verification_receipt.py checks that every required protocol is declared, that recorded receipts are complete, and that the commit named really exists in this history and leads to HEAD. Staleness is reported, never enforced. A receipt is an account of a run, not a substitute for a test CI could have run itself.

docs-instruction-sweep.command: See docs/development/instruction-verification.md -- the full sweep executes every RUNNABLE instruction in the corpus, in the environment each one needs, and records a verdict per block.
docs-instruction-sweep.result: 162 runnable instructions verdicted, zero UNVERIFIED: 95 PASS-AS-WRITTEN, 63 FIXED-DOC, 1 FIXED-CODE, 3 DOCUMENTED.
docs-instruction-sweep.evidence: Per-block verdicts, evidence strings and durations are in docs/development/instruction-ledger.json, which is tracked and gated by tests/test_doc_instructions.py. The CI smoke subset (14 of 162 instructions, 13.8 s measured) rides the projects job and covers command surface only -- it cannot catch wrong-order documentation, which was the dominant defect this sweep found.
docs-instruction-sweep.rationale: The full sweep needs clean virtual environments per chain, network access, a node runtime and roughly an hour of wall clock. CI runs a measured 14-instruction subset instead; the rest is operator-verified and accounted for here.

subprocess-coverage.command: See the [tool.coverage.run] comment in pyproject.toml -- the six fixture studies run with the subprocess coverage hook enabled.
subprocess-coverage.result: Fixture-scope coverage 7% -> 24% once the subprocess hook is active; study loop 80 s uninstrumented, 89 s parent-only, 159 s subprocess-hooked.
subprocess-coverage.evidence: Measured during phase 6, plan 06-04. The parent-only figure is near-meaningless because the stages run as subprocesses, which is what the 7% number shows. The coverage config's `patch=` option was probed and proven to measure nothing silently.
subprocess-coverage.rationale: Deliberately not carried by CI: doubling the study loop's runtime would buy a number no consumer reads, since there is no coverage threshold or upload by design. Recorded here so the figure has a provenance instead of living in a comment.

r7-twin-consumer-identity.command: python tools/r7_twin_consumer_identity.py 7e40a57a 46f2e737 -- captures NetworkModelRepository.load_model(), .validate_integrity() and build_dashboard_catalog() over ONE base directory through each ref's own git worktree, hashes the result, and classifies the difference as identical / additive / regressed.
r7-twin-consumer-identity.result: IDENTICAL - R7 HOLDS. 7e40a57a (pre-Phase-12, the Phase-11 merge) sha256 f209cc7a1486e8258994edfc06f591114720be5da63eebdc6a26f3aa69ddc11c; 46f2e737 (Phase-12 close) sha256 f209cc7a1486e8258994edfc06f591114720be5da63eebdc6a26f3aa69ddc11c. 0 keys added, 0 keys removed, 0 pre-existing values changed. Identity holds THROUGH Phase 12's consumer changes: 12-02 repointed dashboard_catalog's model_version_id from the raw manifest read to model.identity.id, which is value-neutral over this base because the committed manifest's model_version_id equals identity.id -- the verdict measures that equality rather than assuming it. Re-recorded at phase close because 12-02 touched two watched prefixes (gridalyn/twin/network, gridalyn/projects/dashboard_catalog.py) and the previous receipt (recorded 2026-08-12 at 6ed179c0, verdict ADDITIVE d6aa606e->6ed179c0) had gone stale.
r7-twin-consumer-identity.evidence: The digest covers, and only covers: load_model() counts (6 keys), source_adapter, source_standard, provenance_status, every ModelIdentity field, and a content sha256 of each of the five canonical tables (columns, dtypes, rows); validate_integrity() valid/errors/warnings/summary; and the whole build_dashboard_catalog() mapping minus created_at. created_at is stripped because build_dashboard_catalog derives it from datetime.now() -- a pre-existing non-determinism, disclosed in tools/r7_twin_consumer_identity.py rather than hidden. identity.created is NOT stripped: it is read from the base manifest, so it is constant for a fixed base and a code change that stopped propagating it is a real difference. Base fingerprint at the recorded run: metadata.json 6e1b5d1eaee9dfe4f331f546d6097a5aba1aa738dcfb2e3011622c1c35a54e3e, grid_buses 045deb1d1b7092eab0114d88bfae46998a2b90ca092dddb426f1834c8770476e, grid_lines 5e7c9f36028c91e8aeb5d032684f1c06ad08431799d3e345302f4b6a62531260, grid_transformers 2194f3a83b83f8f6b17686d3067df9264717ef84a73857e2143ff61e7275a0f3, buildings 1b0831a652e4b9c01f1fa4d754f6226ee2a5b0594e58e6f9339442274df434dc, building_grid_connectivity bb721ab7c63c03617783f79e538161166111e49b479f878485bbf7f756bbf9ac. Vacuity control: each child reports the directory it imported gridalyn from and the parent asserts it lies inside that ref's worktree (this run: /tmp/r7-7e40a57a-xjxypqfe/gridalyn and /tmp/r7-HEAD-z75e_mil/gridalyn), so a capture that silently read the main checkout fails instead of reporting a perfect match against itself. The determinism control (same ref captured twice yields the same digest) was established on the 2026-08-12 run; this run's cross-ref equality over two independent worktrees is consistent with it.
r7-twin-consumer-identity.rationale: CI cannot run this. The base parquets are gitignored, so a runner has no base to capture over, and regenerating one produces a different created_at and therefore a different digest -- the comparison would measure the regeneration rather than the code. The protocol also needs full git history and two working trees. It is cheap for an operator (~40 s) and is the check to re-run whenever anything under `watched` moves; the gate will report it STALE, which is the intended signal, not a failure.

measured-state-ingest.command: .venv/bin/python tools/measured_ingest_proof.py -- feeds datasets/hq's real measured time axis (35,041 15-min instants, 2018-04-03 to 2019-04-03) and real 1000-entity set through the SHIPPED gridalyn.twin.observation.ingest.read_measured_observations in ONE whole-frame call (35,041,000 tidy rows, no batching -- whole-frame processing is what keeps the shipped duplicate-detection semantics honest), with an operator-declared demo join (EntityJoin.from_mapping, hq_home_{col} -> bus_{col}).
measured-state-ingest.result: 35,041 NetworkObservation(provenance='measured') emitted, one per real instant, as_of spanning 2018-04-03T00:00:00+00:00 to 2019-04-03T00:00:00+00:00; ingest 237.7 s, total 239.6 s, peak RSS 7.6 GB on the operator machine. This proves MECHANICS AT SCALE on real measured timestamps and entities through the shipped path unchanged -- it does NOT prove real voltage data: datasets/hq carries no voltage channel, so the voltage VALUES were synthesized (numpy.random.default_rng(42)) and value-level correctness is proven separately by the CI-visible fixture tests in tests/test_measured_ingest.py. The stored axis is a naive uniform grid with no DST fold, read as UTC; this receipt makes NO DST claim. The entity-to-bus join is operator-declared demo configuration written by the proof script, never inferred.

evidence.axis_reading_disclosure: naive uniform grid read as UTC; no DST fold present in the data -- tz_localize('America/Toronto') raises AmbiguousTimeError and choosing offset policies would manufacture evidence, so the axis is localized with tz_localize('UTC') (lossless, policy-free) and no DST claim is made
evidence.synthesis_disclosure: voltage VALUES are SYNTHESIZED (1.0 + small deterministic variation, numpy.random.default_rng(42)): datasets/hq carries per-home consumption/heating kW and weather, NO voltage channel, and NetworkObservation's measured-mappable field is bus_voltage_pu -- relabeling kW as voltage would fabricate data. This proof claims mechanics-at-scale on real measured timestamps and entities, never real voltage data.
evidence.join_disclosure: the entity-to-bus join is operator-declared demo configuration written by this script (EntityJoin.from_mapping, hq_home_{col} -> bus_{col}); HQ's anonymous ordinal columns carry no key into the twin's bus namespace, so nothing is inferred

measured-state-ingest.rationale: CI cannot run this: datasets/hq is gitignored operator-local data (consumption.h5 ~268 MB) that never ships, and the whole-frame year-at-scale run needs ~7.6 GB of RAM and ~3.5 minutes of wall clock. The at-scale proof of the measured path is therefore operator-verified and accounted for here (R20 criterion: an operator-verified proof case exists for the measured path); the shipped path's value-level behaviour stays CI-proven by tests/test_measured_ingest.py. Re-recorded at the review-cycle-1 fix commit: the first record pinned a commit that predated the proof script itself (born stale), and the cycle-1 fixes changed the shipped ingest path (missing-timestamp rejection), so the full run was re-executed against the fixed path and re-pinned where script and code coexist.
